evidence_frontier: Exp020 promoted Alpha5 (8,550 params) with 897 aggregate Q.ANT correct on ECG200 test (1000 predictions). Exp021 evaluated a 4,278‑parameter w8 compression candidate that achieved 887 aggregate correct, 10 fewer than control, and a w12 candidate (6,414 params) with 884 correct. Both were compared against the same w16 control (8,550 params, 897 correct).
analysis: Observation 1: The w8 candidate (local_width=8) consistently fell 10 correct predictions short of the w16 control across the preregistered seed set (aggregate 887 vs 897). Observation 2: The w12 candidate performed worse (884 correct). Observation 3: No other architectural changes were introduced; training used the ECG200 training split and evaluation used the ECG200 test split. Observation 4: The prior gate was a relative aggregate‑correct threshold (candidate_correct ≥ control_correct − 10).
hypothesis: The w8 local‑width boundary observed in Exp021 is reproducible: when trained and evaluated under identical conditions (same seeds, 50 epochs, ECG200 dataset), the w8 candidate will achieve an aggregate Q.ANT correct count that meets the same relative gate (≥ control_correct − 10).

proposal.title: Confirmation of w8 Local‑Width Boundary on ECG200
proposal.research_question: Is the w8 local‑width compression boundary reproducible under the original training regime, yielding aggregate Q.ANT correct predictions within 10 of the w16 control?
proposal.rationale: Exp021 provided a single‑run indication that a 4,278‑parameter w8 model is 10 correct predictions shy of the promoted Alpha5 w16 baseline. Independent confirmation is required before accepting the w8 boundary as a reliable size‑accuracy trade‑off. The experiment will directly test reproducibility using the preregistered seed set, epochs, and dataset, avoiding any test‑set training leakage.

procedure: For each seed, train a model with the specified local_width (w8 candidate or w16 control) on the ECG200 training set (100 samples) for exactly 50 epochs using identical hyper‑parameters as Exp021.
After training, evaluate the model on the ECG200 test set (100 samples) and record the number of correct Q.ANT predictions (aggregate over the 10 seeds yields a denominator of 1000 predictions).
Do not perform any training on the test set.
Store aggregate correct counts for each candidate.

proposal.risks: Potential risk that stochastic training variance exceeds the 10‑prediction margin, leading to a false negative confirmation. Mitigation: use the exact same seeds and training schedule as the original experiment to minimize variance. No hardware‑level risks because the experiment runs on Q.ANT CPU/software simulation.
